name: jm-chambers
description: Pairs with flows/jm-chambers.json. Tests a REFUSAL, which inverts the usual logic: here the interstitial APPEARING is the pass, and a run that sailed through to a Full Trial would mean the gate is not holding. Only the task-specific items live here; the universals come from _base. Note how few claims are left for a human — the content ones are now string assertions over the a11y snapshot, which the loop was already holding and used to throw away.

items.claim: No request failed except the DESIGNED 402 on the trial route
items.falsifiedBy: any 4xx/5xx that is not a 402. The 402 IS the gate working; anything else on this path is the gate breaking. Overrides the base item, which would fail on the expected refusal

items.claim: A Full Trial was actually requested (not a Quick Ruling by accident)
items.falsifiedBy: no `full trial requested` chapter — the form submitted something else and the gate was never asked the question

items.claim: GUARD — the bench refused and offered chambers instead
items.falsifiedBy: no `chambers offered` chapter. Either the gate let a second Full Trial through (the ledger is not holding) or the refusal arrived too slowly to have preceded the spend, which is the entire point of the downgrade

items.claim: The downgrade was OFFERED, not applied silently — the user had to accept it
items.falsifiedBy: no `chambers accepted` chapter, i.e. a ruling appeared without anyone choosing it. A submit that quietly ran something smaller than what was asked for is a worse betrayal than the paywall it replaced

items.claim: The chambers hearing actually produced a ruling
items.falsifiedBy: no `chambers ruling landed` chapter — the consolation prize does not exist, which is worse than refusing outright

items.claim: The refusal speaks like a bench, not like a SaaS
items.falsifiedBy: the offer screen carrying the bench's line would be absent. Product #6C: every seam the user meets is in-world or the theatre cracks

items.claim: Nowhere in the run does the product say 'quota', 'limit reached' or 'upgrade to Pro'
items.falsifiedBy: any of that copy on screen at any point. The in-voice check above proves the right words are present; this proves the wrong ones are not, which is the half a positive check cannot cover

check.match: quota|limit reached|upgrade to pro|try again tomorrow

items.claim: The chambers ruling carries a real case number, not the JM-LIVE-PREVIEW placeholder
items.falsifiedBy: the placeholder on screen — the ruling was never persisted, so there is no permalink and no record

items.claim: The chambers ruling is COMPLETE — no unlock teaser, nothing withheld
items.falsifiedBy: an unlock/upgrade teaser under a truncated charge list. That would reproduce the exact failure the downgrade replaced, one tier down and invisibly

items.claim: The stored record carries paywallExempt:true — the mechanism fired, not merely the appearance of completeness
items.falsifiedBy: the field absent on the persisted review. Completeness could then be an accident of the daily counter rather than the exemption, and would break the day the counter moved
